title: YUKI model, skill and runtime catalogue
description: Pointers to models (on Hugging Face), skills, and the runtimes models run on (from their projects' own GitHub releases) that YUKI can download. No weights live in this repo. schemaVersion 1; a breaking change gets a new file (catalogue.v2.json) so installed apps keep reading this one. Apps ignore fields they do not know, so adding an optional field is not breaking.

voices.description: Voices for voice models that learn a voice from reference clips (Qwen3-TTS). Optional: apps before it ignore it.

runtimes.description: Optional (apps from before it ignore it): the programs models run on, fetched on demand.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes, up to 64, not ending in a dot. Unique across models, skills and voices. Skill ids become folder names, so a name Windows keeps for devices (con, prn, aux, nul, com0-com9, lpt0-lpt9, with or without an extension) is refused.

tier.description: Hardware tier, from the best NVIDIA card and the RAM: S (24 GB card and 64 GB RAM) > A (20 GB card and 32 GB RAM) > B (12 GB card) > C (8 GB card) > D (no usable NVIDIA card). A card that misses its tier's RAM falls to the next tier it meets (a 24 GB card with 32 GB RAM is A, with 16 GB RAM B).

relativePath.description: Forward slashes, no leading slash, no empty, '.' or '..' parts, no drive letters. Every part must be a name Windows can make: none of \ : * ? " < > | or control characters, not ending in a dot or a space, and not a device name (con, prn, aux, nul, conin$, conout$, com0-com9, lpt0-lpt9, with or without an extension).

summary.description: A few plain sentences: what the user may do, and the catches. Shown before the download.

revision.description: The commit the file is pinned to. Never a branch name.

dest.description: Where it goes, relative to the user's models folder. Never a .part name: that is what YUKI calls a download that is not finished.

moe.description: A mixture-of-experts brain on llama.cpp: what its GGUF is made of, so first run can size it before it downloads and the launch can split it between the card and RAM (every block on the card, the experts of the first N blocks in RAM). `npm run catalogue -w @yuki/desktop -- --facts` reads it from the file's header on Hugging Face and prints this block. Only for kind llm on runtime llama.cpp.

expertLayers.description: Blocks that hold experts, the last ones (default: every block). At most layers.

expertBytes.description: Every expert tensor together (blk.N.ffn_{gate,up,down}_exps): what may wait in RAM.

gpuBytes.description: What never leaves the card: attention, norms, routers, the output head.

embdBytes.description: The token embeddings (llama.cpp keeps them in RAM).

kvBytesPerToken.description: KV cache bytes per token of context with a q8_0 cache, over every block with attention.

contextLength.description: The context it was trained for, in tokens.

registryId.description: The model registry entry these files complete.

gated.description: Needs the user's own Hugging Face login.

rank.description: A brain's place among brains: higher is better, and the highest that fits a PC is the one first run gives it (copies of one model, sharing a registryId, share it). About the size, in billions of parameters, of a dense model as good as it (a dense 27B: 27; Qwen3 30B-A3B: about 10). Without one: 0, the bigger download first.

tags.description: Card tags it starts with in the picker (personal, uncensored...), beside the ones YUKI gives every card.

voice.description: A .zip with profile.json ({ name, clips: [{ file, emotion, lang, text }] }) and the WAV clips it names. YUKI downloads it from the voice card after the user has read the licence summary, which must say where the voice comes from.

url.description: The .zip, https (a file in this repo's voices/ folder, next to the page that says where the voice comes from).

models.description: Voice model ids that can speak with it.

url.description: A SKILL.md or a .zip of the skill's folder.
A project's own GitHub release asset or tag source archive, nothing else.

into.description: Folder inside the runtime's folder it unpacks into (default: the folder itself). One top folder inside the archive is dropped.

runtime.description: Which slot it fills. uv builds the Python environments ComfyUI and Strata run in.

minDriver.description: Oldest NVIDIA driver it runs on.

needs.description: Runtime ids it is set up with.

archives.description: Unpacked in order. Empty only when a setup step does the whole install.

check.description: A file in the runtime's folder that shows it is installed.

setup.description: What YUKI runs after unpacking: comfy = Python environment, PyTorch and ComfyUI's packages; strata = Strata's own setup.

diskGb.description: Disk it takes once set up (archives unpacked plus what setup adds).

experimental.description: Its setup has not been proven on a fresh PC: offered, and said so.
